clue.text: See 10
In this old region you can't see the death of the nation

indicators.note: the death of a word is its final letter, which we are told cannot be seen, so it is dropped

parts.note: a nation can be called a race, a people of common descent

explanation.surface: A lament that in some ancient land you will never witness a people's extinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you' is a link word. Thrace was an ancient region of the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient territory in the southeast Balkans, now split among Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

clue.text: Forty-one theatre jobs coming round — they do come out in spring!

definitions.text: they do come out in spring!

indicators.note: one set of letters comes round, enclosing, the other

parts.note: operations performed in an operating theatre are ops
XLI is forty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Stagehands' work surrounds something that blooms each spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' points to the stage but means the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxlips are primula-family wild flowers that bloom in spring.

clue.text: One cwt frolic this North American native might get involved in

parts.note: one can be the indefinite article a

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together, so this signals a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written: the abbreviation for hundredweight

explanation.surface: A hundredweight beast romping about, the sort of game a native animal might join.
explanation.walkthrough: Start with A (for 'One') and add the letters of CWT FROLIC; rearranging all ten gives the animal. 'this' and 'might' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic wolf is a white subspecies of grey wolf native to northern Canada and Greenland.

clue.text: Means by which to search for lout

explanation.definitionFit: Yahoo is a web search engine; a yahoo is also a boorish oaf, from the brutish creatures in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Slightly advanced sweet

parts.note: A stands for advanced, as in A level
a trifle is a layered custard-and-sponge pudding, a sweet

explanation.surface: Someone has moved a little ahead in the dessert course.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream; in Britain a 'sweet' is a pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning a little or somewhat, as in feeling rather tired.

clue.text: Someone religiously expecting person with a drill to cover this number

indicators.note: one piece covers, enclosing, the other

parts.note: a dentist wields a drill; the a in the phrase gives the article
the clue is 5 down, and five in Roman numerals is V

explanation.surface: A believer waiting for the dentist to cover a certain number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this number' refers to the clue's own number, 5, so V goes inside A DENTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventists are Christians who await the imminent second coming of Christ.

clue.text: Call for something to confirm marriage

definitions.meaning: a band exchanged at a wedding

explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to telephone; a wedding ring seals a marriage.

clue.text: See 28
Estimates losing us after southwest banker's critical interpretations

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: a banker is a river (it has banks), and the Exe flows through Devon in southwest England

indicators.note: the word us is taken out of the estimates

parts.note: estimates are guesses
taken as written

explanation.surface: Figures dropping after a West Country banker gives his learned analyses.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river; 'losing' takes U and an S out, scattered, leaving five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is the critical explanation of a text, especially scripture; this is its plural.

clue.text: What's old catholic Biblical teacher getting into?

indicators.note: one piece gets inside the other

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic
Eli was the priest who taught the boy Samuel

explanation.surface: Asking what an elderly Catholic scripture teacher is up to.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, an old object.

clue.text: Wilde's reported bigamy's apparently the 12 as 17 honeymooning fatwa I've collected

definitions.text: Wilde's reported bigamy's apparently the 12 as 17

indicators.note: the letters are gathered and recollected into a new order

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's quip on bigamy, collected from a religious edict on newlyweds.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilde's line: bigamy is having one wife too many, and monogamy is the same. 12 is SAME, 17 is MONOGAMY.
explanation.definitionFit: The witticism defines bigamy as one spouse more than needed, which it claims also describes monogamy.

clue.text: Gas restricts endless fruit service for babies at Christmas

indicators.note: the outer piece hems in, restricts, the inner one

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas

indicators.note: the fruit loses its final letter

parts.note: an apricot is a fruit
RN is the Royal Navy, an armed service

explanation.surface: Tear gas confines a fruit-serving operation for infants at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like the verb to chatter, but it is the tear gas; 'service' is the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: People born from late December to mid-January have the star sign Capricorn, so Christmas babies qualify.

clue.text: It's Enigmatist (as it's Enigmatist)

parts.note: it is sex appeal, SA
the setter refers to himself, so ME

explanation.surface: A setter naming himself twice, in a riddle about identity.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is the definition: the word repeating 'It's Enigmatist' is the word for identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something twice over shows it is identical, the meaning of the word ditto.

clue.text: Clean, young, yet disturbed correspondent?

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed, thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone tidy and youthful yet troubled writes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An advice columnist answering readers' letters about personal problems is a correspondent of sorts.

clue.text: "28 15 7 20" (anon): this orderly knew I'd cadge

indicators.note: put in order, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An anonymous quotation, and a hospital orderly who admits to scrounging.
explanation.walkthrough: The anonymous quote is THE MOST DANGEROUS FOOD A MAN CAN EAT; 'this' points to the thing it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke saying names this dessert as the most perilous food, since eating it means marrying.

clue.text: See 28
In a spot, letter has extremist angles from the Observer's point of view

definitions.text: angles from the Observer's point of view

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a zit is a spot or pimple
mu is a Greek letter

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the word has

explanation.surface: A pimple-ridden letter-writer with extremist views on angles in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: MU goes in A ZIT, then the outer letters of 'has' follow. The Observer is a British Sunday paper, but here an observer is anyone looking.
explanation.definitionFit: An azimuth is a horizontal angle measured round from north to a sighted object.

clue.text: 10 24 — high record flipped

indicators.note: the two pieces swap round from their clue order

parts.note: a mono record has single-channel sound
game that is high is gamy, strong-smelling

explanation.surface: A tall record turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' swaps 'high record' to give record then high.
explanation.definitionFit: Having just a single spouse is the state of marriage to one partner only.

clue.text: "Drifting life forms look to zap!" (News, in shock)

indicators.note: letters in a state of shock are jumbled

parts.note: new is N, so news is two Ns

explanation.surface: A breaking story says the drifting creatures look ready to be blasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word: the two Ns join LOOK TO ZAP in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms drifting in water; the animal ones are this.

clue.text: Sham subscription in work raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, backwards
one piece goes in the other

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
dues are a membership subscription

explanation.surface: A fake membership fee within a piece of work is put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reads the assembled letters upwards, as suits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo as an adjective means false or pretended.

clue.text: See 28
Second leg, so expose buttocks

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
in cricket, the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A second leg, so time to bare one's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side and the on side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooning is the prank of baring one's backside.

clue.text: Country in which blouse is confused with sari

indicators.note: the letters are confused, mixed together

explanation.surface: A nation where shirts and saris get mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which', 'is' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Belorussia is an older name for Belarus, a country in eastern Europe.

clue.text: Public, in the course of time

parts.note: over can mean during, as in over the weekend

explanation.surface: Something public over a period.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and not concealed, done in public view.

clue.text: See 10
It's inhaled to set in motion means of controlling BP

indicators.note: letters set moving are shuffled about

explanation.surface: A drug that is breathed in to start lowering blood pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link. BP is blood pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorthalidone-type diuretics like this are drugs used to treat high blood pressure.

clue.text: Channel for cast to broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: to cast is to shoot, as a fishing line or a glance

explanation.surface: A TV channel looking for actors to air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' and 'broadcast' suggest television, but the channel is a slide or trough.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping passage down which things slide, a channel.

clue.text: Bashful's quality attempt to hit head

parts.note: a shy is a throw at a target, as at a coconut shy
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Bashful, one of the dwarfs, defined by a trait of trying to strike someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being timid and easily embarrassed is the defining trait of a bashful person.

clue.text: 14 amusement arcades? Fandango too hot to handle

indicators.note: letters handled are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Amusement arcades and a Spanish dance prove too hot to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted saying is anonymous; 14 is WEDDING CAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke saying describes wedding cake as perilous because it commits the eater to marriage.
